JUDGMENT
This claim petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by her in a road traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioner is as follows:-
That on 23.04.2025 at about 11.30 p.m., the petitioner being an occupant of Car bearing No. KA-02- MT-4195 was traveling in the said vehicle with other passengers and when they were going near Pipeline, Chowdeshwarinagara under pass,
Kamakshipalya, at that time the driver of said car drive the same in a rash and negligent manner and took sudden right turn and hit to the Car coming from opposite direction, result of which, the petitioner sustained injuries.
Immediately the petitioner was shifted to Chord Road Hospital, Bangalore wherein admitted as an inpatient for a period of one week.

So far, the petitioner has spent Rs.3,00,000/-
towards medical expenses and other incidental charges.
3. Prior to the accident, petitioner was hale and healthy.
She was working as Tailor and earning sum of Rs.30,000/- per month.
Due to the permanent disability petitioner is not in a position to do the said work.
She has suffered pain and sufferings, permanent disability, loss of income, loss of future income and other pecuniary and non-pecuniary damages.

4. The Respondent no.1/the insurer of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-02-MT-4195 has filed written statement and admitted the coverage of insurance policy and the liability if any subject to the terms and conditions mentioned in the policy.
The respondent no.1 has contended that the driver of the insured vehicle was not holding valid driving license and the said vehicle was not having permit.
It is further contended that there is one day delay of lodging the complaint.
5. On Service of notice, the respondent no.2 appeared through his counsel but has not filed written statement and thereby uncontested the petition.

6. On the basis of the above pleadings the following points arise for the consideration of the court:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that he met with a motor vehicle accident on 23.04.2025 at about 11.30 p.m., on Pipeline road, Chowdeshwarinagara under pass,
Kamakshipalya and sustained grievous injuries due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-02-MT-4195 ?

7. The petitioner got examined herself as Pw1 and one witness is examined as P.W.2 and got marked documents as per Ex.P1 to Ex.P13.
The respondents did not adduced the evidence.

8. Heard arguments and perused the materials.
9.

My findings on the above issues are as follows:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative Issue No.2: Partly in the affirmative.
Issue No.3: As per final order, for the following;

REASONS 10. ISSUE No.1 : - In order to explain the actionable negligence of the driver of offending vehicle,
P.W.1 has filed his affidavit explaining the vivid picture of the accident that took place on 23.04.2025 at about 11.30 p.m., when the petitioner being an occupant of Car bearing No.
KA-02-MT-4195 (hereinafter referred to as the offending vehicle) was traveling in the said vehicle with other passengers and when they were going near Pipeline, Chowdeshwarinagara under pass,
Kamakshipalya, at that time the driver of the said Car drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and took sudden right turn and hit to the Car coming from opposite direction, result of which, the petitioner sustained injuries.

P.W.1 further deposed about the nature of injuries sustained, treatment taken and the amount spent for treatment etc.
11.

In support of the claim and to prove the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle , the P.W.1 has relied upon Ex.P1 to 7 which are the police records such as F.I.R with complaint,
statement, spot mahazar, sketch, IMV report, wound certificate and charge sheet etc.
12.

On the basis of the complaint lodged by Sharath S, case has been registered against the rider of offending vehicle in Crime No 138/2025 of Kamakshiplaya Police Station for the offence punishable under section 281, 125(a) of BNS.

The Investigation officer after investigation has filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offence punishable under Section 281, 125(b) of BNS 2023.
13.
Respondent No.2 is the owner/driver of the offending vehicle in which petitioner was traveling.
Respondent No.2 is none other than the son-in-law of the petitioner.

The complaint was lodged against the respondent no.2 by the driver of the Car bearing No.KA- 02-MT-4195 which was also involved in the accident, alleging that rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is the cause for the accident.

Accordingly, FIR was filed against the respondent No.2 and after investigation charge sheet was filed against him.

sentences.text: If the spot mahazar and sketch is perused, at the time of accident the offending vehicle was proceeding from Sunkadakatte towards Kamalanagar.
The Car was proceeding from opposite direction i.e., from Kamalanagar towards Sunkadakatte.
The width of the road at the spot of accident is nearly 40 feet and it is two way road.

The sketch discloses that the respondent No.2 by driving the offending vehicle from the left side of Kamalanagar- Sunkadakatte Road took the vehicle towards extreme right side of the said road and hit to the vehicle of the complainant which was proceeding from Kamalanagar towards Sunkadakatte on the left side of the said road.
Hence, from the topography of the scene of occurrence it can be said without any hesitation that the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is the sole cause for the accident.

If really accident in question has occurred other than the manner one stated by the petitioner, then definitely the respondent No.2 would have contested the case by filing written statement, by cross examining the PW.1 and by leading his evidence.

Further, apart from the complaint lodged by the driver of another vehicle involved in the accident, even the petitioner has given her statement as per Ex.P2 wherein she has clearly stated that the respondent No.2 who is her son-in-law was driving the offending vehicle under drowsiness in a rash and negligent manner and hit to the another vehicle coming from the opposite direction.
Hence, the materials placed on record clearly proves the issue No.1.

Hence,
issue No.1 is answered in the affirmative.
15. ISSUE No.2:-
The petitioner has given evidence to the effect of her sustained grievous injuries.
As observed earlier, petitioner has produced medical documents which are at Ex.P6 and Ex.P8.
On going through the medical documents it reveals that petitioner has taken treatment as an inpatient from 24.04.2025 to 26.04.2025 at Chord Road Hospital for a period of 3 days.
As per the wound certificate the petitioner has sustained one injury which is grievous in nature.
16. Dr. S.A.Somashekara, Orthopedic Surgeon at Victoria Hospital, Bangalore is examined as PW.2 and through him OPD card with examination report and x-ray film are got marked as Ex.P12 and Ex.P13.
PW.2 has deposed that he examined the petitioner on 05.12.2025 for disability assessment.
PW.2 further deposed that petitioner has suffered permanent physical disability of left lower limb at 36% and on whole body at 18%.
PW.2 stated that petitioner need surgery for removal of implant which would cost around Rs.40,000/- in private set up.
17. If the cross examination of PW.2 is perused, admittedly PW.2 has not given treatment to the petitioner at any point of time.
The fracture injury is united and petitioner was advised to take physiotherapy treatment.
As per the evidence of PW.2, even though joints are normal but movement is not normal and petitioner can do her day to day activities with difficulties and there is no shortening of limbs.
Further as per the own evidence of PW2.
the petitioner has sustained 36%of disability on right lower limb.

The PW.2 having assessed the disability on particular limb at 36%,
assessed the disability on whole body at 18%.

As per judgment reported in 2014 (4) Kar.L.J 157 Vijaya Kumar Alias Babu Rao Vs The Secretary, Agricultural Produce Marketing Committee Balki,
Taluk the normal rule would be disability in the lower limb would be 1/3rd of the particular limb.

sentences.text: Taking in to consideration the nature of injuries sustained, period of treatment taken, this court is of the opinion that petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads.
19. Towards pain and sufferings, petitioner shown to have sustained one grievous injury.

Hence taking in to consideration the nature of injury sustained by the petitioner and time taken for treatment and sufferings during the treatment it is reasonable to hold that petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.75,000/- towards pain and suffering.
20. So far as the medical expenses incurred by the petitioner is concerned, she has produced 15 medical bills for Rs.1,65,383/- as per Ex.P.10.
Hence petitioner is entitled for Rs.1,65,383/- under the head medical expenses.
21. It is stated that petitioner was 48 years and she was working as Tailor and thereby earning sum of Rs.30,000/- per month.
To substantiate the said contention the petitioner has not produced any materials.

Hence considering the age of the petitioner, the year of accident and place of residence this court considers the income of the petitioner at Rs.17,000/- p.m.
22.
The petitioner has sustained grievous injury and taken treatment for 3 days as inpatient at Chord Road Hospital, Bangalore.
Hence the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner which is grievous in nature it is reasonable to hold that period of three months as complete laid down period.
Hence petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.51,000/- towards loss of income during the laid down period.
23. From the evidence of Pw1 and as borne out by medical records, petitioner has taken treatment for several times.
Further for 3 days of hospitalization requires an attendant, was traveled to hospital for treatment.
She has taken nourishment and need further nourishment at this age and incurred other incidental expenses.
Therefore all together incidental expenses is assessed at Rs.25,000/- taking in to consideration the cost of living and value of money during the year 2025.
24. The petitioner has contended that she is aged about 48 years as on the date of accident.
Petitioner has produced Ex.P9/Aadhar card which shows her date of birth as 21.03.1976.
That means petitioner was aged about 49 years.
Hence considering the Aadhar Card this court has taken the age of the petitioner as 49 years.

25. So taking in to consideration the monthly income of the petitioner having considered by this tribunal as Rs.17,000/- p.m. and if 12% of loss of earning capacity is considered and when the age of the petitioner at the time of accident was 49 years, as per Sarla Varma's case the multiplier applicable to the age group of 46 to 50 is '13'.
So by applying the multiplier '13' the future loss of income due to disability comes to Rs.3,18,240/- (i.e., 17,000 x 12% x 13 x 12 )-.
Hence this Tribunal holds that the petitioner is entitled for Rs.3,18,240/- towards future loss of income due to disability.
26. PW.2 has stated that petitioner has to undergo one more surgery for removal of implant.
The approximate cost might be around 40,000/-.
in private set up.
The PW.2 has not stated the estimated cost of future surgery and has not given estimation.

Hence, this court inclines to award Suvarnamma vs Universal Sampo Gen Ins Co Ltd on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/177703654/

sentences.text:
future medical expenses only to the tune of Rs.25,000/-.
27.
The petitioner at her age of 49 years has suffered grievous injury and permanent disability.
Hence it may cause some amount of loss of amenities and discomfort.
Hence this court inclines to award sum of Rs.30,000/- under the head loss of amenities and discomfort.

Thus Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
 Sl. No Heads Amount Rs.
1. Towards pain & sufferings Rs.75,000/-
2. Medical expenses Rs.1,65,383/-
3. Towards loss of income during Rs.51,000/-
 laid up period 4.

Towards Conveyance, Rs.25,000/-
 Attendant charges and  nourishing food 5. Loss of Future Income Rs.3,18,240/-
6.

Future medical expenses Rs.25,000/-
7. Loss of comfort and Rs.30,000/-
 amenities  Total Rs.6,89,623/-

Therefore this court holds that petitioner is entitled for Rs.6,89,623/- (Rupees Six Lakhs Eight Nine Thousand Six Hundred Twenty Three only).
28.
As regarding liability is concerned, there is no dispute that offending vehicle was insured with 1st respondent and policy was in force as on the date of accident.
The respondents remained absent and they have not led any evidence.
29. Hence it can be said that all the documents pertaining to the offending vehicle was valid and in force as on the date of accident.

Hence by fastening liability on the respondent no 1 this court directs the respondent no.1 to pay compensation to the petitioner along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of accident till the date of payment of entire amount.
Accordingly Issue No. 2 is answered.
30. ISSUE No.3:-
In the light of findings given on Issue No.1 and 2, my finding on this Issue is as per the following final order.

sentences.text: The claim petition filed by the petitioner is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The petitioner is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.6,89,623/- + cost of Rs.1,000/- imposed vide order on IA No. III.
The petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.6,90,623/- (Rupees Six Lakhs Ninety Thousand Six Hundred Twenty Three only).
A Sum of Rs.6,64,623/- shall also carry interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The Respondent No.1 is directed to deposit the compensation along with interest within two months from the date of award.

On deposit of the said amount 50% of compensation payable to the petitioner shall be deposited in her name in any nationalized bank of the choice of petitioner for a period of 3 years and the remaining 50% shall be released to the petitioner through E-payment on proper identification.
Advocates' fee is fixed at Rs.1, 000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
